summary: Round 5 should stay on the existing static vanilla-JS app and preserve clipboard parsing, saved-player sidebar, 6-candidate generation, candidate ranking, hidden internal balance scores, and click-to-swap editing. The new scope is a focused UX pass: compress the current 10-player + preference area into dense row-based summaries, add a visible one-click reroll for the 6 candidate cards without clearing current inputs, and surface a natural GitHub issue contact path in the main UI and docs.

milestones.title: Compact Current Match Panel
milestones.objective: Replace the tall per-player preview cards with a dense, row-first current-roster view that still supports per-player 6-point preference editing and quick comparison.
deliverables: Refactor `src/lib/render.js` `renderPreview()` and the current per-player renderer so the `현재 10명 확인 및 선호 점수` section renders 10 compact `current-player-row` style items instead of tall `roster-card` blocks.

Each current-player row must show, in one glance, the player name, preference source state (`기본 2 / 2 / 2`, `저장 불러옴`, `직접 조정`), the three role tier tokens, and inline tank/damage/support preference controls with visible integer values.
Keep the existing `preference-minus-*` and `preference-plus-*` id pattern so `src/main.js` preference binding can be preserved with minimal logic churn.
Add a dedicated dense-list wrapper in `renderPreview()` such as a capped-height `current-player-list-scroll` container so the preview section no longer becomes a stack of 10 large cards.

Update `src/styles.css` with compact current-player row classes, smaller chips/steppers, tighter vertical spacing, truncation rules, and responsive behavior that avoids horizontal overflow without returning to tall card layouts.
Update the preview-related copy in `src/constants/copy.js` so the Korean guidance matches the new dense summary layout and still makes clear that balance score numbers remain hidden from the main UI.

milestones.title: Candidate Regenerate UX
milestones.objective: Let the user quickly generate another set of 6 candidate teams from the same current roster and preference state without re-pasting input or disturbing saved-player selection.
deliverables: Add a visible `후보 6개 다시 생성` action to the result-section header in `src/lib/render.js`, positioned near the candidate summary so it reads as part of the recommendation workflow.
In `src/main.js`, extract the current candidate-generation state assignment from `handleBalance()` into one shared helper so both `팀 나누기` and reroll use the same code path.

Implement `handleRegenerateCandidates()` in `src/main.js` so reroll rebuilds candidates from `state.matchPlayers` only; it must not clear or rewrite `state.clipboardText`, `state.matchPlayers`, `state.savedPlayers`, or `state.savedPlayerSelectionIds`.

On reroll, replace the current candidate list and editor with the fresh `buildBalanceFromPlayers(state.matchPlayers)` result and reset the editor to the newly ranked candidate 1. Previous manual swap state should be discarded because the result set has been regenerated.
Do not change `src/lib/optimizer.js` ranking precedence. Reroll is a new entry point into the existing randomized tie-bucket selection and preference-weighted surfacing, not a scoring-rule rewrite.
Keep the result panel free of numeric balance labels after reroll; the new action must not expose team totals, score differences, or internal metric names.

milestones.title: Inquiry CTA And Shell Polish
milestones.objective: Add a visible support/contact path to the main UI and keep the top-level Korean copy aligned with the new round-5 behavior.
deliverables: Add visible inquiry text and a clickable link to `https://github.com/haskell26/team-builder/issues` in the main shell via `src/lib/render.js` and `src/constants/copy.js`. Place it in a naturally visible area such as the hero, side guidance panel, or footer note inside the main UI.
Make the inquiry line actual user-facing Korean text, not a hidden developer note and not a README-only instruction.
Refresh result/guide copy so the UI explains that users can compare 6 compact candidates, reroll them quickly, and still edit the selected candidate below.
Preserve the existing saved-player sidebar information architecture from round 4; this milestone is copy/shell polish only, not another saved-player layout rewrite.

milestones.title: Regression Coverage And Handoff Docs
milestones.objective: Lock the round-5 UX changes with deterministic tests and leave README/FINAL_OUTPUT aligned with shipped behavior.
deliverables: Extend `test/appFlow.test.js` to cover dense current-player row rendering after paste/load, preference editing from the compact row layout, reroll button presence, reroll preserving textarea/current-player state, and visible GitHub issue guidance in the app shell.

Add deterministic reroll verification. Prefer a controlled `Math.random` sequence or a small test helper so one app-flow test can prove the result area is recomputed without relying on flaky randomness.

Update `test/responsiveLayout.test.js` to assert the compact current-player list container, row-level dense styling hooks, capped-height behavior, and no regression in the saved-player sidebar or candidate/editor responsive contracts.

Keep existing regression coverage for header/headerless parsing, exact-10 saved-player loading, candidate ranking order, 6-candidate output, unique player assignment, candidate selection, swap editing, and hidden-score rendering. Extend only where round-5 behavior touches them.

Update `README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` to describe the new dense current-match UI, the reroll workflow, and the GitHub issue contact path. Keep verification notes truthful: `npm test` and `npm run build` are required, while browser/mobile smoke remains optional and non-blocking unless actually executed.
Run `npm test` and `npm run build` before handoff and record the results in the docs.

acceptance_criteria: After a valid 10-player paste or saved-player load, the `현재 10명 확인 및 선호 점수` section renders 10 compact current-player rows instead of 10 tall card-style entries.
Each current-player row shows the player name, preference source state, three role tier summaries, and current tank/damage/support preference values with editable controls.
The current-match preview uses a dense layout and a capped-height or equivalent compact container so the section no longer stretches the page like a stack of large cards.
Preference editing still works from the compact row layout, and each player's tank/damage/support total remains exactly 6 after every change.
The main UI still hides internal balance numbers such as personal tier score, team total, total score difference, role-score difference sum, tank score difference, and unranked difference.
When candidates are available, the result section shows a visible `후보 6개 다시 생성` button.
Clicking the reroll button recalculates candidates from the current roster and current preference-point state without requiring the user to paste input again.
Reroll does not clear or rewrite the textarea contents, current-player rows, saved-player library, or saved-player selection count.
After reroll, the result section still shows exactly 6 candidates and the final editor reflects the freshly selected candidate set.

Candidate ordering still follows total score difference, then role-group score-difference sum, then tank score difference, then unranked distribution difference, with randomness only inside exact metric ties.
Every displayed candidate still assigns 10 unique players and keeps both teams at `1탱 2딜 2힐`.
Selecting a candidate still loads it into the final edit area, and clicking two slots still swaps players immediately.
The saved-player sidebar remains collapsed by default and exact-10 saved-player load gating still works after the round-5 changes.
The main UI visibly includes inquiry text plus a clickable link to `https://github.com/haskell26/team-builder/issues`.
`README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` both mention the reroll workflow, dense current-match UI, and GitHub issue contact path.
Header-present and headerless clipboard input both still parse correctly.
All new user-facing text introduced in this round remains in Korean.
test_strategy: Extend `test/appFlow.test.js` so the main entrypoint test asserts compact current-player rows after paste, preference controls still mutate values and source state, and the UI no longer depends on tall preview cards.

Add an app-flow reroll test that controls randomness explicitly, clicks `팀 나누기`, captures the result markup, clicks `후보 6개 다시 생성`, and asserts the result area is recomputed while `textarea.value` and current-player UI state stay intact.
Add or update assertions that the main shell HTML contains the GitHub issues URL and visible Korean inquiry text.

Update `test/responsiveLayout.test.js` to verify the new current-player dense-list classes, capped-height container, truncation rules, and mobile-safe shrink/wrap behavior without horizontal overflow.
Keep optimizer regression tests for ranking precedence and tie-bucket randomization so reroll work cannot accidentally change scoring order.
Keep parser, saved-player, candidate selection, swap editing, and hidden-score regression coverage in place; add only the minimum extra assertions needed for round 5.
Run `npm test` and `npm run build` as required verification. Treat `npm run test:browser` as optional and only claim it in docs if it was actually executed.

risks.risk: The dense current-player row layout can become too cramped, making preference controls hard to use or causing overflow with long Korean names and tier text.
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing plus/minus interaction model, add explicit compact row/grid CSS with `min-width: 0` and truncation, and cover the layout contract in `test/responsiveLayout.test.js`.

risks.risk: The reroll action can accidentally clear clipboard input, current preferences, or saved-player selection if it reuses the wrong reset path.
risks.mitigation: Extract candidate generation into a helper that only rewrites result/editor state, and add an app-flow test that asserts textarea contents and preview state are unchanged after reroll.

risks.risk: Users may click reroll and sometimes see little visible change if the current roster has few exact-metric ties.
risks.mitigation: Keep the button labeled as a fresh regenerate action rather than promising a completely different result every time, and verify recomputation deterministically in tests with controlled randomness.

risks.risk: A builder may modify optimizer ranking rules while wiring reroll because the new feature touches candidate generation code.
risks.mitigation: State explicitly that `src/lib/optimizer.js` ranking precedence must stay unchanged and retain the existing optimizer ranking tests as a guardrail.

risks.risk: The GitHub issue guidance may be added in a low-visibility place or only in docs, failing the main-UI requirement.
risks.mitigation: Place the CTA in top-level shell rendering, assert the URL and Korean inquiry copy in app-flow tests, and mirror the same guidance in `README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md`.

risks.risk: The workspace still contains round-4 `.harness` artifacts, which can cause implementation drift if the builder follows stale wording instead of this round-5 plan.
risks.mitigation: Treat this plan as the authoritative round-5 execution source, and ensure the shipped docs and handoff explicitly describe the dense current-match UI, reroll UX, and issue guidance introduced in this round.

definition_of_done: The current 10-player preview is rendered as a dense row-based summary view that supports the existing 6-point preference editing workflow.
The current-match section no longer expands as 10 large cards and remains visually compact for normal desktop use.
The result section includes a visible reroll action that regenerates 6 candidates from the same roster and preference state without clearing inputs.
Candidate ranking precedence, hidden internal balance scores, saved-player sidebar behavior, candidate selection, and click-to-swap editing all still work.
The main UI includes a visible GitHub issue inquiry link for questions and suggestions.
Automated tests cover the dense current-player rows, reroll preservation behavior, and inquiry link presence, along with existing parser/optimizer/editor regressions.
`npm test` and `npm run build` pass before handoff.
`README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` describe the shipped round-5 behavior and keep browser/mobile verification notes honest and non-overclaimed.
open_questions: Assumption: the round-5 prompt in this task supersedes the older round-4 wording currently present in `.harness/spec.md` and `.harness/plan.json`.
Assumption: the reroll button only needs to be shown when a valid candidate set already exists; the empty result state can remain simple.
Assumption: reroll resets the selected candidate/editor to the newly ranked candidate 1 and clears prior manual swap state, because the candidate set has been regenerated.
Assumption: the compact current-player rows should reuse inline plus/minus controls rather than introducing free-form numeric text inputs, to minimize state and validation changes.

Assumption: desktop should remain one-row-first for each current-player summary; on narrower widths, limited internal wrapping is acceptable as long as the UI stays compact and does not regress to tall card stacks.
Assumption: prior browser/mobile real-device verification gaps remain non-blocking in this round, but the docs must still state exactly what was and was not executed.
